title: Every Breath You Take
headline: Sting says this famous love song is 'sinister and ugly.'
caption:
"It sounds like a comforting love song. I didn't realise at the time how sinister it is." That's Sting on the song he wrote in half an hour after waking in the night with the line in his head. He'd started it at Ian Fleming's writing desk in Jamaica, where he'd gone to escape the public eye.

The lyrics are the words of a possessive lover, watching every breath and every move. Sting thinks he had Big Brother, surveillance and control in mind. In 1988, sociologist Gary T. Marx called it "a love rather than a protest song" but said it "nicely captures elements of the new surveillance," linking its lines to breath analysers, ankle monitors and voice stress analysis.

None of that stopped it topping the Billboard Hot 100 for eight weeks, the Police's only No. 1 there. In 2003, VH1 ranked it the No. 2 greatest breakup song.

Love song or watching-you song: which do you hear?

🎧 The song: "Every Breath You Take" by The Police (@thepolicebandofficial)
